items.title: Association between changes in the cardiometabolic index and new-onset cardiovascular diseases in middle-aged and elderly individuals: findings from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study.
items.abstract: Cardiometabolic index (CMI) is a new obesity and lipid metabolism-related index consisting of anthropometric and biochemical index. Our study aimed to examine the association between CMI control level and cardiovascular diseases (CVD) risk in middle-aged and elderly individuals. A total of 4,239 subjects were enrolled from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS). The K-means clustering model and cumulative CMI to assess change in the CMI from 2012 to 2015. The association between CMI change and new-onset CVD was evaluated using Cox regression models and restricted cubic splines (RCS). Subgroup analyses and interaction tests were conducted to evaluate potential relationships between changes in CMI and outcomes across different subgroups. There were 872 subjects eventually developed CVD, including 652 cases of heart disease and 352 cases of stroke. New-onset CVD was positively and independently correlated with changes in CMI. Subjects with consistently high CMI had a higher new-onset CVD risk. The higher cumulative CMI was associated with a stepwise increase in outcomes. RCS showed the correlation between cumulative CMI and outcomes was nonlinear. Sustained high CMI was related to an elevated risk of new-onset CVD in middle-aged and elderly population. Continuous CMI monitoring significantly enhances the accuracy of new-onset CVD risk stratification, potentially lowering CVD incidence.

items.title: Global burden of pulmonary arterial hypertension in infants under 1 year, 1990-2023, and projections to 2040: a GBD 2023 analysis.
items.abstract: Using GBD 2023 data, we updated the global burden of infant PAH (1990-2023) and analyzed incidence, disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), and mortality by region, sex, age, and sociodemographic index (SDI). Trends were analyzed via joinpoint/log-linear regression, with ARIMA forecasting to 2040. The incidence remained stable (0.18 per 100,000, EAPC -0.04%), while DALYs and mortality declined (EAPCs -3.40%, -5.36%). Improvements were unequal: high-SDI regions fell most, and low-SDI regions experienced increasing cases and the slowest DALY reduction. India had the highest number of cases/deaths, and Afghanistan had the highest DALY rate. In half of the patients, mortality peaked at 6-11 months. The incidence of mortality was slightly greater for girls than for boys, and boys had greater DALYs/mortality. Projections to 2040 show persistent burden (DALYs 49.29, mortality 0.52 per 100,000) and unchanged sex disparities. Despite overall progress, socioeconomic inequalities remain. The stable incidence and increasing low-resource burden call for targeted, equitable interventions focusing on low-SDI countries, the perinatal period, and new-born males.

items.title: Association between systemic inflammatory response index and the severity of coronary artery lesions in patients undergoing coronary angiography for the first time.
items.abstract: Inflammation drives coronary artery disease (CAD). The systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) reflects systemic inflammatory status, yet its association with CAD severity in first-time coronary angiography patients remains unclear. This retrospective study included 219 inpatients undergoing initial coronary angiography. CAD severity was quantified by the Gensini score. Patients were divided into SIRI quartiles. Spearman correlation, multivariable linear regression, logistic regression, and ROC analyses were performed. Median Gensini scores increased across SIRI quartiles (Q1: 16.75, Q2: 44.00, Q3: 40.00, Q4: 52.00; P   P   β  = 0.177, 95% CI: 0.089-0.266, P   β  = 0.080, 95% CI: -0.021 to 0.182, P  = 0.121). Each SIRI unit increase was associated with 2.44-fold higher odds of an above-median Gensini score (>42) (OR = 2.438, 95% CI: 1.544-3.851, P  < 0.001). SIRI showed modest discrimination for an above-median Gensini score (AUC: 0.685, 95% CI: 0.615-0.755), numerically the highest among the seven indices but not statistically superior to NLR, SII, or PIV. Subgroup analyses confirmed significant correlations across sex, age, diabetes, and hypertension strata. SIRI is positively associated with angiographic CAD severity in patients undergoing first-time coronary angiography. As an inexpensive biomarker derived from routine blood counts, SIRI may serve as an adjunctive tool for pre-procedural risk stratification in this specific population.

items.title: Machine learning-based prediction of in-hospital and post-discharge mortality in heart failure: an international retrospective study with cross-endpoint transferability analysis.
items.abstract: Patients with heart failure (HF) face substantial morbidity and mortality. This study aimed to build machine learning (ML) models for predicting in-hospital or post-discharge mortality in acute decompensated HF and explore whether models trained on one mortality endpoint transfer to the other. Two retrospective HF cohorts were analyzed: 40,265 patient encounters from 15 hospitals in the United States (USA) with in-hospital mortality (3.6%) as the endpoint, and 4,892 encounters discharged alive from five hospitals in Greece (GRC) with 1-month all-cause mortality (9.2%) as the endpoint. ML models were trained using either all available features in each cohort (full models) or only variables shared between cohorts (restricted models), enabling both within-endpoint internal validation and cross-endpoint transferability assessment to be performed. During within-endpoint internal validation, discrimination was strong for the full USA models and moderate for the full GRC models, with extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) reaching an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.85 and 0.70, respectively. Advanced age and elevated admission blood urea nitrogen were the most consistent predictors. In the cross-endpoint transferability analysis, restricted XGBoost models applied to the opposite cohort retained above-chance discrimination but were significantly outperformed on the same test set by the models developed for that cohort's endpoint. In two international cohorts of patients with acute decompensated HF, post-discharge mortality in the GRC cohort was more challenging to predict than in-hospital mortality in the USA cohort. XGBoost models developed for one mortality endpoint retained a degree of discriminative ability on the other endpoint, suggesting a partially shared prognostic signal between in-hospital and post-discharge mortality, while confirming the expected superiority of endpoint-specific models.

items.title: Early blood pressure, cardiac biomarker, and strain changes for risk stratification of cardiovascular toxicity during VEGFR-TKI therapy: a cardio-oncology cohort study.
items.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors (VEGFR-TKIs) have become integral to the treatment of several solid tumors but are associated with a distinctive spectrum of cardiovascular toxicity, particularly hypertension and myocardial dysfunction. Because vascular and myocardial abnormalities may emerge soon after treatment initiation, we evaluated whether early changes in blood pressure, cardiac biomarkers, and echocardiographic strain could provide complementary information for cardio-oncology risk stratification. We analyzed a retrospective cohort of 640 adults initiating axitinib, sunitinib, pazopanib, sorafenib, or lenvatinib. Baseline cardiovascular risk factors, prior cardiotoxic therapy, blood pressure, high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI), N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were assessed, with repeat evaluation at 4 weeks. The primary outcome was the first clinically significant cancer therapy-related cardiovascular toxicity (CTR-CVT) within 12 months, encompassing treatment-emergent or worsening hypertension requiring treatment escalation, cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), heart failure, clinically significant arrhythmia, or arterial thromboembolism. Cox regression and fixed-horizon discrimination analyses were performed. The cohort had a mean age of 60.5 ± 11.4 years; 360 (56.2%) were men and 255 (39.8%) had baseline hypertension. Mean systolic blood pressure increased from 129.8 to 143.2 mmHg, while mean GLS changed from -19.0% to -17.7% at week 4. During 12 months, 155 patients (24.2%) experienced the composite outcome. In a multivariable Cox model, age (HR 1.023 per year, 95% CI 1.008-1.038), week-4 systolic blood pressure (HR 1.018 per mmHg, 95% CI 1.008-1.029), and relative GLS decline (HR 1.042 per percentage point, 95% CI 1.000-1.085) were associated with the outcome. Adding week-4 blood pressure, GLS, hs-cTnI, and NT-proBNP changes to baseline variables increased the 12-month AUC from 0.638 to 0.693. The AUC estimates describe apparent performance within the analyzed cohort, without internal or external validation. Early vascular and myocardial changes after VEGFR-TKI initiation provided complementary information beyond baseline clinical risk. Week-4 systolic blood pressure and relative GLS decline were the strongest independent dynamic markers, while biomarker changes added more limited incremental information after mutual adjustment. These findings support multimodal early surveillance during VEGFR-TKI therapy and warrant prospective external validation before use for treatment decisions.

items.title: Dual Adenosine-Modulating Nanoparticles for Metabolic-Epigenetic Reinvigoration of Antitumor Immunity.
items.abstract: Tumors co-opt extracellular adenosine (eADO) signaling and intracellular N6-methyladenosine (m 6 A) demethylation to evade CD8 + T cell immunity, creating dual immunotherapy barriers. Single-pathway targeting remains inadequate due to compensatory crosstalk. Here, we engineer core-shell structured dual adenosine-modulating nanoparticles (DAMNs) for sequential response to microenvironmental cues and site-specific agent delivery. DAMN shells disintegrate in the tumor microenvironment to release a CD73 inhibitor, blocking eADO generation and adenosine receptor signaling. Meanwhile, the cores deliver an FTO (fat mass and obesity-associated protein) inhibitor intracellularly, abrogating m 6 A demethylation-dependent upregulation of programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and antioxidant defense. In colorectal and triple-negative breast cancer models, concerted CD73 and FTO inhibition synergistically lowers interstitial eADO, dually disrupts the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, disables tumor redox adaptation, and enhances CD8 + T cell recruitment and activation, driving potent tumor suppression and preventing post-surgical relapse and metastasis. This spatiotemporally orchestrated platform introduces a therapeutic paradigm to simultaneously overcome immune evasion and impose intrinsic metabolic-epigenetic vulnerability for enhanced cancer therapy.

items.title: Role and intervention strategies of metabolic-epigenetic cross-talk in the treatment of drug resistance in colorectal cancer.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) continues to be one of the most prevalent gastrointestinal malignancies on a global scale. Despite advancements in targeted therapy and immunotherapy that have enhanced outcomes for certain patients, primary and acquired drug resistance remain significant challenges that impede clinical efficacy. Metabolic reprogramming is widely acknowledged as a fundamental hallmark of cancer, facilitating survival advantages for tumor cells by restructuring glucose, amino acid, and lipid metabolic networks. Critically, this reprogramming directly fosters a drug-tolerant phenotype by modifying the flux of metabolic intermediates. Simultaneously, aberrant epigenetic modifications-including the remodeling of DNA methylation, altered histone acylation, and dysregulated non-coding RNA networks-play an indispensable role in the establishment and maintenance of resistance to targeted therapies in CRC. Notably, metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic remodeling do not function independently. Recent research indicates that cellular metabolites serve as substrates or cofactors for the regulation of epigenetic modifying enzymes. Conversely, alterations in the epigenome feedback to regulate the transcription of metabolic enzymes. This interplay establishes a bidirectional regulatory mechanism.

items.title: Left Parotid Gland Metastasis as the Initial Presentation of Pulmonary Adenocarcinoma: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Parotid gland metastasis from pulmonary adenocarcinoma is exceptionally uncommon and may closely mimic a primary salivary gland malignancy. We report a 48-year-old heavy smoker who presented with progressive left parotid swelling, facial pain, and mild facial weakness without respiratory symptoms. FDG PET-CT demonstrated an FDG-avid left parotid lesion and suspicious right upper lobe pulmonary abnormalities, followed by MRI characterization of the deeply seated parotid mass. Fine-needle aspiration was classified as Milan Category V, suspicious for malignancy, and a subsequent parotid core biopsy demonstrated poorly differentiated carcinoma with CK7, TTF-1, and Napsin A positivity, supporting pulmonary differentiation. The patient subsequently underwent left parotidectomy with neck dissection, and histopathology confirmed metastatic carcinoma in the deep parotid lesion. Subsequent bronchoscopy and infectious investigations were non-diagnostic. CT-guided biopsy of a right upper lobe lesion confirmed pulmonary adenocarcinoma with an acinar growth pattern. Molecular testing showed no EGFR mutation, negative ALK and ROS1 immunohistochemistry, no pathogenic DNA variants or gene fusions on targeted next-generation sequencing, CDKN2A copy-number loss, and PD-L1 expression <1% in the lung specimen. With the parotid gland as the only documented extrathoracic metastatic site and no intracranial metastasis, the disease was classified as M1b (stage IVA). The patient received carboplatin, pemetrexed, and pembrolizumab and achieved a qualitative partial metabolic response on follow-up PET-CT; treatment was complicated by grade 2 hepatitis/transaminitis and grade 1 dermatitis requiring corticosteroids and temporary interruption of immunotherapy. At approximately four and a half months after treatment initiation, the patient remained clinically stable while receiving maintenance pemetrexed and pembrolizumab. This case highlights the diagnostic value of integrating imaging, immunophenotyping, molecular characterization, and histopathological confirmation of both sites.

items.title: The tau-microtubule axis in Alzheimer's disease: reciprocal mechanisms, biomarker gaps, and therapeutic challenges.
items.abstract: Microtubule dysfunction has been implicated in axonal transport failure, synaptic degeneration, and neuronal loss in Alzheimer's disease, yet its position within the disease process remains unresolved. This critical narrative review evaluates the tau-microtubule axis across physiological, pathological, biomarker, and therapeutic contexts. Tau interacts dynamically with microtubules and regulates labile domains, motor access, severing, intracellular transport, and neuronal compartmentalization rather than acting solely as a constitutive stabilizer. In Alzheimer's disease, abnormal post-translational modification, somatodendritic mislocalization, and aggregation alter these functions and may disrupt axonal transport, mitochondrial trafficking, and synaptic maintenance. Conversely, experimental microtubule disruption can release tau and promote its subsequent phosphorylation. These findings motivate a proposed reciprocal framework in which tau abnormalities and microtubule dysfunction may amplify one another, with potentially stage-dependent contributions from amyloid-β-tau interactions, neuroinflammation, altered tubulin modifications, and metabolic stress. Cellular and animal models support several components of this framework, but direct causal evidence in humans remains limited. Tau-lowering therapies, immunotherapies, kinase-directed interventions, and microtubule-modulating agents have shown variable outcomes, with molecular target engagement not consistently translating into clinical benefit. Current tau biomarkers measure soluble phosphorylation changes or aggregate burden but do not directly assess microtubule integrity, tau-microtubule binding, or axonal transport competence. This biomarker gap limits mechanistic interpretation of clinical trials and prevents adequate testing of whether therapeutic target engagement restores the neuronal functions that these interventions are intended to preserve.

items.title: Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor: a misdiagnosis-prone tumor with immune checkpoint expression and immunotherapeutic implications.
items.abstract: Epithelioid trophoblastic tumor (ETT) is the rarest form of gestational trophoblastic neoplasia and is highly prone to misdiagnosis due to its morphological overlap with squamous cell carcinoma and epithelioid leiomyosarcoma. It is also relatively chemoresistant, and effective therapies for recurrent or metastatic disease remain lacking. We retrospectively analyzed five ETT cases, integrating clinicopathological review, immunohistochemistry for diagnostic markers (GATA-3, p63, p40, p16) and immune checkpoints (PD-L1, PD-L2, B7-H3, VISTA), and multiplex immunofluorescence to resolve spatial co-expression. Four cases were initially misdiagnosed. p40 was focally positive in all five ETT cases, with diffuse strong positivity in SCC controls, highlighting a potential diagnostic pitfall. PD-L1 CPS ranged from 10 to 60; PD-L2 and B7-H3 were predominantly expressed on tumor cells, with B7-H3 showing the highest positivity. VISTA was largely confined to CD3+ immune cells, with only rare tumor-cell expression. Multiplex immunofluorescence revealed frequent co-expression of B7-H3, PD-L1, and PD-L2 on GATA-3+ tumor cells, with triple-positive cells ranging from 5% to 35% across cases, indicating co-expression of multiple immune checkpoint molecules.A. These findings refine diagnostic awareness and provide a pathological rationale for immunotherapy in ETT. The immune checkpoint co-expression pattern supports further evaluation of combination immunotherapeutic strategies in this rare, chemoresistant malignancy.

items.title: Gut microbial characteristics associated with pegylated interferon treatment response in chronic hepatitis B: insights into the gut-liver axis.
items.abstract: Pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) treatment response varies considerably among patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The role of the gut microbiota in this heterogeneity remains unclear. This study aimed to characterize gut microbial features associated with Peg-IFN response and explore their potential relevance to the gut-liver axis. A total of 64 patients with CHB who completed 24 weeks of Peg-IFN-based therapy were enrolled in this study. Fecal samples collected at week 24 were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Microbial characteristics and clinical factors associated with treatment response were evaluated, followed by development of an integrated classification model. Among the 64 patients, 38 were classified as responders and 26 as non-responders. Responders exhibited distinct gut microbial profiles, characterized by increased microbial richness ( p  = 0.014), altered community composition ( p  = 0.045), and different microbial interaction patterns. Dorea abundance was enriched in responders and independently associated with treatment response. Multivariable logistic regression identified lower baseline HBsAg levels (OR = 0.562, p  = 0.048), higher platelet counts (OR = 1.020, p  = 0.007), and increased Dorea abundance (OR = 3.876, p  = 0.008) as independent factors associated with response. Restricted cubic spline analysis supported a significant association between Dorea abundance and response probability. The Virological-Host-Microbial (VHM) triad model integrating these factors demonstrated promising apparent discrimination (ROC-AUC = 0.790) and calibration in the development cohort. Distinct gut microbial ecological patterns are associated with Peg-IFN treatment response in CHB, with Dorea representing a characteristic microbial feature. This study provides a multidimensional framework for understanding heterogeneity in interferon responsiveness and highlights the potential relevance of the gut-liver-immune axis.

items.title: Determining the effectiveness of integrating hepatitis B, C, and HIV using an integrated care model to optimize uptake of screening among pregnant mothers attending antenatal clinics in West Nile Sub-Region, Uganda.
items.abstract: perinatal transmission of hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) from an infected mother to the baby is an important route of transmission. HBV and HIV prevalence are 3.8% and 3.1%, respectively, in the general population in the study area, with no HCV prevalence established. Screening pregnant mothers in the first trimester using the integrated care model (ICM) leads to identification of infections and reduces the risk of transmission to the unborn baby. This study set out to evaluate the effectiveness of integrating HBV, HCV and HIV to optimize screening among participants attending the antenatal clinic (ANC) in the West Nile Region, Uganda. a quasi-experimental study design was conducted with intervention (705) and control (691) groups, respectively. One thousand, three hundred and thirty-eight participants were recruited and screened at the ANC. A structured questionnaire and laboratory register were used for data collection. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and generalized linear model (GLM) with identity link function and binomial family to estimate the percentage difference of HBV and HIV screening between the two groups. Categorical and continuous variables were compared across the comparison groups. The propensity score (PS) model to estimate the IPTW weights was fitted for comparing only two groups. there was a significant impact of the intervention on screening, awareness, and vaccination (p<0.05). Screening for HBV and HIV was 652 (92.5%) in the intervention group and 623 (90.2%) in the control group. Awareness of HBV, HCV, and HIV risks during pregnancy was also significantly higher in the intervention group, 640 (92.4%), compared to the control group, 487 (70.7%). The majority of the participants accessed information from the ANC. the need for early detection of HBV, HCV, and HIV in the first trimester, reduction of 'lost opportunity' and HIV risk awareness, screening, and HBV vaccination at one point of care underscores the necessity of ICM.

items.title: Distinct plasma proteomic trajectories during PD-1 blockade and PEG-IFNα therapy are associated with HBsAg response in chronic hepatitis B.
items.abstract: PD-1 blockade and pegylated interferon-α (PEG-IFNα) are promising immunomodulatory strategies for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), but their systemic immune effects and response-associated proteomic patterns remain poorly defined. We performed longitudinal plasma proteomic profiling using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel in 25 nucleos(t)ide analogue-suppressed patients with CHB receiving PD-1 blockade (n=10) or PEG-IFNα (n=15). Plasma samples were collected at baseline, week 12, and week 24. Longitudinal protein changes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models, and associations with week-24 HBsAg decline were evaluated using responder-non-responder comparisons and Spearman's rank correlation. Responders were defined by an HBsAg decline of ≥1 log 10 IU/mL at week 24. Seventy-seven proteins passed quality-control criteria. PEG-IFNα induced substantially broader longitudinal proteomic remodeling than PD-1 blockade, with most changes occurring within the first 12 weeks. Treatment-by-time analyses identified distinct trajectories between therapies, including differential changes in IL-18R1, TNF, CX3CL1, CXCL9, and CXCL10. Response-associated analyses suggested treatment-specific patterns: IL-10 was the leading exploratory signal in the PD-1 cohort, whereas IL-12B, CDCP1, and FGF-21 were more prominent in the PEG-IFNα cohort. These response-related associations did not remain significant after false discovery rate correction and were therefore considered exploratory. PD-1 blockade and PEG-IFNα induce distinct longitudinal circulating inflammatory proteomic programs in CHB. Favorable HBsAg decline was accompanied by treatment-specific rather than universal proteomic signatures, supporting the potential value of longitudinal proteomics for mechanistic and biomarker studies of HBV functional-cure strategies.
items.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

items.title: Liver-Targeted Tolerogenic Lipid Nanoparticles for Treating Autoimmune Diseases.
items.abstract: Autoimmune diseases affect an estimated 4-9% of the global population, yet current therapies remain predominantly non-specific, offering symptom control rather than durable immune correction. The convergence of liver immunology and lipid nanotechnology offers a mechanistically grounded route toward organ-specific, antigen-directed immune tolerance, an approach that aims to reprogram, rather than merely suppress, pathological immune responses. Liver-resident antigen-presenting cells, including Kupffer cells, liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, and tolerogenic dendritic cells can be selectively engaged by engineered lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) to promote the generation of antigen-specific regulatory T cells and reprogram inflammatory networks. Preclinical studies across murine models of autoimmune hepatitis, type 1 diabetes, and multiple sclerosis demonstrate significant disease attenuation, including expansion of FoxP + regulatory T cells and reduction of pathogenic effector responses, alongside favorable safety profiles, particularly when LNP design emphasizes liver-restricted targeting and controlled antigen release. This review provides a critical analysis of the immunological basis of liver tolerance, encompassing Kupffer cell, liver sinusoidal endothelial cell, tolerogenic dendritic cell, and regulatory T cell networks, and evaluates the physicochemical design principles of liver-targeted tolerogenic LNPs at the intersection of immunology and nanomedicine, with particular emphasis on surface engineering, cargo co-delivery strategies, and stimuli-responsive release mechanisms that have not been comprehensively reviewed in prior work. We further discuss the physicochemical design principles governing nanoparticle biodistribution, cellular uptake, and immunomodulatory function, and evaluate current preclinical and emerging translational evidence. Finally, we address key challenges, including targeting specificity, off-target immunotoxicity, and regulatory considerations, and outline future directions such as combination tolerance strategies and next-generation nanoparticle engineering. Together, liver-targeted tolerogenic LNPs offer a potentially transformative approach, opening possibilities for scalable clinical translation.

items.title: Incisional hernia repair after abdominal organ transplantation: current evidence, controversies and research gaps.
items.abstract: Incisional hernia is a common late complication of abdominal organ transplantation, with reported frequency ranging from a pooled 4% after kidney transplantation to a prevalence of 43% on clinical examination after liver transplantation. Immunosuppression places recipients at least in Ventral Hernia Working Group grade 2, and concern about wound failure, mesh infection and recurrence often delays repair. This mini review synthesises evidence on elective repair in adult liver, kidney and pancreas recipients around three questions: whether transplant status independently predicts adverse outcome, how immunosuppression relates to outcome, and how operative access, reconstruction, mesh plane, material and fascial closure should be chosen. In most registry and matched comparisons, 30-day wound morbidity and length of stay were similar to those of non-transplant patients, although one matched laparoscopic series found more surgical site occurrences. Study-specific recurrence ranges from 0% in selected specialist series to 37%, with differing follow-up and ascertainment, and observational comparisons do not establish whether transplantation independently increases recurrence. A randomised trial showed more wound complications with de novo sirolimus after kidney transplantation; the association between maintenance sirolimus and recurrence after later repair rests on small, conflicting series, and perioperative conversion is untested. Recent series of transversus abdominis release report recurrence of 0%-25%, depending on incision, defect size, follow-up and comparator. Diaphragmatic tack fixation should be avoided. Two randomised trials of prophylactic mesh at transplant closure are registered, without published results. Research priorities include transplant-specific registry fields, standardised recurrence ascertainment, longer post-repair follow-up and graft-related outcomes.
items.journal: Journal of abdominal wall surgery : JAWS

items.title: Evidence-gated integration of microbiome, metabolome, and host transcriptome data reveals a gap between reproducible signals and cross-layer mechanistic evidence in hepatocellular and colorectal cancer.
items.abstract: Microbiome multi-omics studies frequently identify microbial, metabolic, and host transcriptional associations, but their reproducibility and support for connected biological mechanisms remain uncertain. We evaluated these relationships in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) using an eight-dimensional, non-compensatory evidence-gating framework. Nine public HCC datasets spanning microbiome, metabolome, and host transcriptome profiles were analyzed alongside CRC microbial and metabolomic data and separate host transcriptomic datasets. Analyses included cross-cohort replication, participant-matched taxon-metabolite associations, host transcriptional responses, sensitivity testing, and independent evidence scoring. Complete mechanistic eligibility required support across all eight evidence dimensions. In HCC, 13 genera showed concordant directions and nominal significance across conventional leave-one-cohort-out analyses, but none met the adjusted external validation criterion. Six longitudinal plasma feature-window signals and 12 differential liver metabolites were identified without cross-specimen concordance under false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Three hepatic transcriptional programs replicated across independent bulk datasets, but none of the four HCC candidate families met all eight evidence requirements. In CRC, four bacterial species replicated in held-out disease-feature testing. Paired microbial and fecal metabolite profiles from 347 participants yielded 18 replicated taxon-metabolite associations, of which 10 met robustness criteria and eight retained support after joint-taxon adjustment. The Peptostreptococcus stomatis-glycocholate association replicated in held-out testing (adjusted residual r = 0.315, q = 0.00232) and remained significant after joint-taxon adjustment (β = 0.209, q = 0.0144) and unified-partition analysis with global Benjamini-Hochberg correction (held-out q = 0.0303). Reanalysis of glycocholic acid (GCA) treatment transcriptomic data identified increased SOX14, ZDHHC9, and CD274 expression, although the three-gene response score yielded an exact permutation P = 0.10. Independent assessments agreed on all 48 evidence ratings (quadratic-weighted κ = 1.000). Evidence gating distinguished reproducible molecular associations from complete cross-layer mechanistic support. The P. stomatis-glycocholate association, accompanied by complementary GCA-responsive host transcription, represents a candidate for further investigation rather than an established microbial-metabolite-host mechanism.

items.title: Risk prediction models for the risk of portal vein thrombosis in patients with liver cirrhosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.abstract: Portal vein thrombosis (PVT) is a common complications of liver cirrhosis. Its occurrence increases the difficulty of clinical management for patients with liver cirrhosis, accelerates disease progression, and raises mortality. Therefore, early prevention, diagnosis and identification of patients with PVT are of vital importance. This study used a meta-analysis to evaluate risk prediction models for PVT in liver cirrhosis, aiming to provide a scientific basis for future model development and clinical application. We searched databases including PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science for relevant literature published from database inception to July 2026. Two researchers conducted the literature screening and data extraction, and used the Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool (PROBAST) to evaluate the risk of bias in the prediction models. Meta-analysis was performed using Stata 14.0. A total of 11 studies were included, involving 8670 participants and 15 prediction models were involved. Two of these prediction models underwent external validation. The PROBAST assessment indicated that all studies were at a relatively high risk of bias, although the prediction models showed good applicability. The area under the curve (AUC) values of these prediction models ranged from 0.608 to 0.919.The pooled AUC of the 15 prediction models was 0.81 (95% confidence interval: 0.78-0.84), indicating fair discrimination. Current evidence suggests that existing prediction models for PVT in patients with liver cirrhosis seem to demonstrate fair discriminatory performance. However, owing to substantial heterogeneity and limited validation and calibration, these models are not yet suitable for widespread clinical application. Future multicenter, prospective studies are therefore warranted.

items.title: Comparison of Classical Image Processing Methods and the Artificial Intelligence-Based MedSAM2 Model for Liver Tumor Segmentation in Radioembolization Dosimetry: A LiTS Dataset Analysis.
items.abstract: Accurate estimation of tumor and critical organ doses in radioembolization therapy is essential for treatment planning. The choice of segmentation technique used in voxel-based dosimetry can affect the calculated volumes and dose estimates. In this study, the liver tumor segmentation performances of classical image processing methods and a pretrained artificial intelligence (AI) Medical Segment Anything Model 2 (MedSAM2) were compared, along with their effects on a simplified dose-change indicator. From the 131 training cases in the Liver Tumor Segmentation Benchmark dataset, 33 eligible cases were identified using previously published radioembolization eligibility criteria; of these, 30 patients were selected by tumor-volume-stratified sampling. In each patient, four classical methods [dilation, erosion, region of interest (ROI)-based Otsu thresholding, ROI-based K-means clustering] and one AI-based method (MedSAM2) were applied to the reference tumor mask, and the resulting volumes were compared with the reference volume to calculate a simplified medical internal radiation dosimetry-derived dose-change percentage. All five methods were successfully completed in all 30 patients. Mean±standard deviation (median) dose-change percentages were -25.5%±8.9% (-25.3%) for dilation, 50.9%±30.2% (43.1%) for erosion, 177.3%±1324.8% (-78.3%) for ROI-thresholding, -65.0%±33.0% (-79.0%) for ROI-K-means, and -30.2%±40.7% (-34.6%) for MedSAM2. ROI-thresholding produced an extreme deviation (7189.2%) in one patient due to a degenerate threshold; MedSAM2 showed a similar extreme deviation (-99.2%) in one patient by segmenting an area approximately 123-fold the reference volume. Excluding these outliers, MedSAM2's variance remained lower than that of the classical thresholding and clustering methods. The choice of liver tumor segmentation method can lead to differences ranging from 10% to over 1000% in simplified dose estimates. Classical thresholding and clustering methods tend to produce infrequent but severe outliers, whereas a pretrained AI model (MedSAM2) yields more stable results, although it is not entirely error-free. These findings point to the importance of standardizing and reporting the segmentation method used in pre-treatment dosimetric assessment for radioembolization. Radyoembolizasyon tedavisinde tümör ve kritik organ dozlarının doğru tahmini, tedavi planlamasının güvenilirliği için kritik önem taşır. Voksel-tabanlı dozimetri yöntemlerinde kullanılan segmentasyon tekniğinin seçimi, hesaplanan hacimleri ve dolayısıyla doz tahminlerini doğrudan etkileyebilir. Bu çalışmada, klasik görüntü işleme yöntemleri ile hazır eğitilmiş bir yapay zeka (YZ) modelinin (MedSAM2) karaciğer tümörü segmentasyon performansları ve bunların basitleştirilmiş doz değişimi üzerindeki etkileri karşılaştırılmıştır. Liver Tumor Segmentation Benchmark veri setinin 131 eğitim olgusundan, önceden yayımlanmış klinik radyoembolizasyon uygunluk kriterlerine göre 33 uygun olgu belirlenmiş, tümör hacmine göre tabakalı örnekleme ile 30 hasta seçilmiştir. Her hastada referans tümör maskesine dört klasik yöntem [morfolojik genişletme, morfolojik daraltma, lokal ilgi alanı (ROI) tabanlı Otsu eşiklemesi, lokal ROI tabanlı K-means kümeleme] ve bir YZ tabanlı yöntem (MedSAM2) uygulanmış, elde edilen hacimler referans hacimle karşılaştırılarak basitleştirilmiş tıbbi iç radyasyon dozimetrisi türevi bir doz değişim yüzdesi hesaplanmıştır. Otuz hastanın tamamında beş yöntem başarıyla tamamlanmıştır. Doz değişim yüzdesinin ortalama ± standart sapma (medyan) değerleri sırasıyla dilation için -%25,5±%8,9 (-%25,3), erosion için %50,9±%30,2 (%43,1), ROI-eşikleme için %177,3±%1324,8 (-%78,3), ROI-K-means için -%65,0±%33,0 (-%79,0) ve MedSAM2 için -%30,2±%40,7 (-%34,6) olarak bulunmuştur. ROI-eşikleme bir hastada dejenere bir eşik değeri nedeniyle aşırı bir sapma (%7189) üretmiş; MedSAM2 ise bir hastada referans hacmin ~123 katı bir alanı segmentleyerek benzer bir aşırı sapma (-%99,2) göstermiştir. Bu tekil aşırı değerler hariç tutulduğunda MedSAM2’nin varyansı, klasik eşikleme/kümeleme yöntemlerine kıyasla belirgin şekilde daha düşük kalmıştır. Karaciğer tümörü segmentasyonunda yöntem seçimi, basitleştirilmiş doz tahminlerinde %10’dan %1000’in üzerine varan farklara yol açabilmektedir. Klasik eşikleme ve kümeleme yöntemleri nadir ama şiddetli aşırı değerler üretme eğilimindedir; hazır eğitilmiş bir YZ modeli (MedSAM2) genel olarak daha kararlı sonuçlar vermekle birlikte tamamen hatasız değildir. Bulgular, radyoembolizasyon öncesi dozimetrik değerlendirmede segmentasyon yönteminin standartlaştırılması ve şeffaf biçimde raporlanmasının önemine işaret etmektedir.

items.title: [Association between circulating insulin-like growth factor-1 and liver health and verification of its predictive efficacy for liver disease risk].
items.abstract: Objective: To study the association between circulating insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) level and the risk for liver diseases as well as liver characteristics, evaluate the potential of circulating IGF-1 level to be used as a novel predictive indicator for liver diseases, and provide scientific evidence for clinical screening and early intervention. Methods: Based on large-scale population data from the United Kingdom Biobank, a total of 371 466 study participants were included in this study. The HR of circulating IGF-1 level to liver outcome and its 95% CI were calculated through the Cox proportional hazards regression model. The prediction of circulating IGF-1 level for different liver disease outcomes was evaluated by using C -index, and the differences in predicting the risks for liver fibrosis and cirrhosis between circulating IGF-1 level and fibrosis index (FIB-4) were compared based on the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results: During the median follow-up period of 13.74 years, 10 507 cases of liver diseases, 295 cases of primary liver cancer, and 928 cases of liver-related deaths occurred. Increased circulating IGF-1 level was associated with decreased risk for liver disease (for every 5 nmol/L increase, the adjusted HR =0.87, 95% CI : 0.85-0.88), and was also associated with decreased risk for primary liver cancer ( HR =0.60, 95% CI : 0.51-0.71) and liver-related deaths ( HR =0.54, 95% CI : 0.50-0.60). Circulating IGF-1 level had acceptable predictive efficacy for nultople liver disease outcomes ( C -index range: 0.57-0.80), with an IGF-1 C -index of 0.80 (95% CI : 0.76-0.85) for hepatocellular carcinoma; the IGF-1 C -index of 0.71 (95% CI : 0.69-0.73) for liver fibrosis and cirrhosis. In the risk prediction for liver fibrosis and cirrhosis, the efficacy of circulating IGF-1 level was superior to FIB-4, with AUC of 0.706 and 0.678 ( P =0.005). Conclusions: Higher circulating IGF-1 level is associated with lower risk for liver diseases, and as a novel biomarker, it shows better efficacy in predicting the risk for liver fibrosis and cirrhosis compared with FIB-4. 目的： 研究循环胰岛素样生长因子-1（IGF-1）水平与肝病风险及肝脏特征的关联，并评估循环IGF-1作为肝病新型预测工具的潜力，为临床筛查和早期干预提供科学依据。 方法： 使用英国生物银行的大规模人群数据，纳入371 466名研究对象进行分析。通过Cox比例风险回归模型计算循环IGF-1水平与肝脏结局的 HR 值及其95% CI ，采用 C 指数评估循环IGF-1对各肝病结局的预测能力并基于受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUC）比较其与纤维化指数（FIB-4）在肝纤维化和肝硬化风险预测中的效能差异。 结果： 在13.74年的中位随访期间，新发肝病10 507名、原发性肝癌295名及肝脏相关死亡928名。循环IGF-1浓度升高与新发肝病风险降低相关（每增加5 nmol/L，回归稀释校正后的 HR =0.87，95% CI ：0.85~0.88），同时与原发性肝癌（ HR =0.60，95% CI ：0.51~0.71）及肝脏相关死亡（ HR =0.54，95% CI ：0.50~0.60）风险下降相关。循环IGF-1对多种肝病结局均具有可接受的预测效能（ C 指数范围：0.57~0.80），在预测肝细胞癌风险时，IGF-1的 C 指数为0.80（95% CI ：0.76~0.85）；在肝纤维化和肝硬化中IGF-1的 C 指数为0.71（95% CI ：0.69~0.73）。在针对肝纤维化和肝硬化的风险预测中，循环IGF-1的效能优于FIB-4，其AUC分别为0.706和0.678（ P =0.005）。 结论： 较高的循环IGF-1水平与较低的肝病风险相关，且其作为新型生物标志物在肝纤维化和肝硬化风险预测中表现出优于FIB-4的效能。.
